title: Choose the visual world for the new Birdcar homepage
question: The roll assigned The quiet tower. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Comps render into each card as they finish.

options.label: The quiet tower
options.lineage: Air traffic control radar, airfield signage, flight progress strips
options.thesis: You're the control tower every task radios; I build the lanes so the tower goes quiet.
options.viewport: A live radar scope where every task spirals into YOU; the hook left, a black-on-yellow airfield sign to book, the canary blip flying in as the Walkthrough.
options.risk: Dark scopes drift toward hacker/sci-fi cliché; it has to stay warm, legible, and owner-plain.

raised.raise: Every work item carries a callsign and fixed fields on a strict cell grid, so the scope and strips read as a real system, not decoration.
The scope is one continuous surface: scrolling reroutes every blip in place, never a before/after image swap.
Lanes wake in sequence like runway approach lights, leading the eye down to the booking sign.
A running tower log records each fix as you descend, so the page keeps an honest record of what changed.
The Walkthrough is a boarding pass whose every field is literally what you get: the hour, the report, Where I'd start, three business days.

options.label: Your business, in miniature
options.thesis: A living 3D model of their business where every task piles onto the owner's desk, until the systems reroute it.
options.viewport: Headline left; a floating cutaway of a small business right, packets converging on the owner's desk, a canary caged beside the pile.
options.risk: Isometric 3D is familiar SaaS territory and can tip cute; the heaviest build and the hardest on phones.

options.label: Constructed clarity
options.thesis: Scattered cells snap into a monumental headline: order as the visible proof of craft.
options.viewport: BETTER WORK, FASTER built from grid cells with its last letters still assembling; one canary-yellow diagonal is the only rebellion.
options.case: Holds product clarity with huge, legible type; loses audience identification, since owners read it as a design-studio poster.
options.risk: Cold and designer-coded; the person behind it can disappear.

options.label: Teletext service
options.thesis: The business as numbered broadcast pages keyed by digits.
options.viewport: A P100 index page with the offer as numbered rows.
options.case: Loses both axes: US owners never lived with teletext, and the bitmap grid buries the offer.
options.kept: Fixed-field, addressable discipline: every item gets a callsign.

options.label: Floated pigment
options.thesis: Every intervention displaces the whole surface.
options.viewport: A liquid bath the visitor combs into figures.
options.case: Loses both axes: beautiful, but says nothing about operations and hides the offer.
options.kept: One continuous surface where a single change visibly propagates.

options.label: Coiled earth tower
options.thesis: A slow ascending record of construction.
options.viewport: Text banded in courses up a tower wall.
options.case: Loses both axes: terracotta craft reads artisan, not Silicon Valley systems.
options.kept: A visible running record of what was built, course by course.

options.label: Bosquet vistas
options.thesis: Axial vistas that break into secret rooms as fountains wake in sequence.
options.viewport: A symmetrical garden plan with the offer on the central axis.
options.case: Loses both axes: grandeur and power fight a personal, practical offer.
options.kept: Orchestrated sequence: things wake in order to lead the eye.

options.label: Ekiben kiosk
options.thesis: The offer as a box whose printed contents map is true.
options.viewport: A lid with the Walkthrough's contents mapped by number.
options.case: Loses both axes: honest and clear, but reads as a food brand and a cream-paper cliché.
options.kept: The promise as a literally true, itemized contents map.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Ramp/Stripe-grade SaaS homepage, played straight at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Centered outcome headline and two buttons over a Systems-that-never-spoke constellation.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every SaaS page; a one-person brand competes with software companies on their own turf.
